name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.114.0 — The four hand-rolled "does this page apply the wireframe register" checks across design-atlas.js and mocks-driver.js now share one derivation, spec/scripts/lib/wire-register.js, which reads a page's applied stylesheets — link tags with a stylesheet rel in any quoting form or attribute order, plus CSS @import, comments stripped — and answers whether any target has wire as a whole path segment, fixing a register applied through @import being read as unstyled and a deleted-but-commented register link being read as drawn. 7.113.0 — The theme pick moves to /spec:sketch's new first-run Theme step — the mocks driver's theme state/compose/open/adopt subcommand family lives outside the mocks state machine, candidates are the signed-off gray kit re-rendered per direction at design/theme/<kebab>/kit.html, and the picked direction's kit page becomes the fidelity reference every later sketch surface is built from; theme adopt supersedes rather than refuses, marking every other confirmed theme: row overridden so exactly one confirmed pick survives across all directions and a later genesis brief is never grounded on two contradictory picks [no-ac: review's version-bump check is the oracle]. 7.112.0 — The release stage's e2e leg now reds on an unobserved run — an observed zero executed count, or a declared count format that never matched — and the journeys leg reds when zero journeys were walked; the count parsers plus the unobserved predicate now live in one shared module that both review-legs.js and release-legs.js import instead of each declaring their own.
